**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — denial of prior authorization for lumbar disc decompression (CPT 63030)**

- **Member:** Morgan Foster
- **Member ID:** W162894592
- **Reference number:** POC-F4C641ED8B-99591
- **Date of denial notice:** August 23, 2026
- **Plan:** Ambetter (Commercial/ACA), State of Illinois
- **Governing policy:** *Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)*, Date of Last Revision: 04/25 — https://www.ambetterhealth.com/content/dam/centene/ambetteril/clinical-policies/CP.MP.114.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the plan's denial of prior authorization for the lumbar disc decompression recommended by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD (orthopedic surgery). The notice dated August 23, 2026 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking for reconsideration, because when I read the plan's own published criteria in *Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)* against my medical records, the records appear to line up with what the policy asks for. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have quoted the plan's criteria exactly as they appear in the policy and matched each one to what is in my chart.

---

### 1. The threshold criteria

The policy states:

> "A. Age ≥ 18 years; B. Dia gnosis of herniated lumbar disc;"

I am an adult. My date of birth is [my date of birth], which is on file with the plan. My diagnosis is a herniated lumbar disc: my MRI of the lumbar spine dated June 26, 2026 shows **L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.**

### 2. Nerve root compression confirmed by imaging

The policy states:

> "C. Ne rve root compression confirmed by imaging and one of the following:"

This is exactly what my imaging shows. The June 26, 2026 MRI documents compression of the traversing L5 nerve root at L4-L5, with severe right lateral recess stenosis. My examination also documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The compression is confirmed by imaging, and it corresponds to my symptoms and my exam findings.

### 3. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit, and failure of conservative therapy

The policy allows the criterion above to be met through the following pathway:

> "2. Radiculopathy with sensory deficit as evidenced by pain, parasthesias or numbness in a nerve root distribution, and member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative ther apy including all the following:"

I have radicular pain in a nerve root distribution: **radicular pain into my right calf**, on the same side as the imaged L5 nerve root compression. I have had 24 months of progressive lower back pain that is not relieved by rest, and I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes.

The policy then lists the conservative care that must be documented. Taking each element in turn:

> "a. ≥ four weeks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or doc umentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

**Met.** I completed supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility — **12 weeks, from April 24, 2026 to July 17, 2026, 18 visits completed**, documented in my physical therapy discharge note. That is substantially more than four weeks.

> "b. ≥ four weeks activity modification; c. One of the following:"

Regarding activity modification, my records document that I cannot stand more than 10 minutes and that my pain has been progressive and unrelieved by rest over 24 months. To the extent the plan requires separate documentation of activity modification for this period, I ask that it be obtained from my treating providers: [records documenting activity modification — dates and description, to be supplied by my provider's office].

For the "one of the following" element, the policy lists:

> "i. NSAID or acetaminophen ≥ three weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated;"

> "ii. Epidural steroid injection."

**Met.** I took **NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief** — far longer than three weeks. In addition, I received a **corticosteroid injection on June 17, 2026, which gave only about 4 weeks of partial relief.**

So on the plan's own sensory-deficit pathway, my records show imaging-confirmed nerve root compression, radicular pain in that nerve root's distribution, more than four weeks of supervised physical therapy, and well beyond three weeks of NSAID therapy, plus an injection that did not hold.

### 4. The motor-deficit pathway

The policy also offers a motor-deficit pathway:

> "1. R adiculopathy with motor deficit and one of the following: a. Severe weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by: a score of ≤ 3 on the Me dical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale, or the inability to ambulate;"

> "b. Mild to moderate weakness in a nerve root distribution, as evidenced by a score of 4 on the Medical Research Council 0 to 5 muscle strength scale and one of the following:"

> "i. Worsening weakness or motor deficit; ii. Member/enrollee has failed to respond to conservative therapy, within the last year, including all of the following:"

> "a) ≥ four wee ks physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program, or documentation of member/enrollee’s inability to tolerate;"

> "b) ≥ four weeks activity modification; c) One of the following:"

> "1) Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) or acetaminophen ≥ thre e weeks unless contraindicated or not tolerated; 2) Epidural steroid inj ection;"

My records state that I have a **neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level**, but they do not record a numeric Medical Research Council muscle strength score. I am not going to claim a grade that is not in my chart. I raise this pathway only to note that the policy requires **one** of the listed findings under criterion C, and that the sensory-deficit pathway above is satisfied on the face of my records. If the plan reviewed my request under the motor-deficit pathway and the absence of a recorded MRC score was the issue, I ask that this be stated, so that Dr. Reyes can supply a strength examination.

### 5. A request about the criteria the plan applied

I want to be straightforward with you about the limits of what I can address. Several of the excerpts I have quoted end in a colon and introduce further sub-conditions that I do not have in front of me, and the policy contains additional criteria that are not reproduced in this letter. The denial notice I received states only that the request "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," without identifying which specific criterion was not satisfied. I am therefore asking the plan to identify, in writing, the exact criterion or criteria from *Clinical Policy: Disc Decompression Procedures (CP.MP.114)* that my documentation was found not to meet. If there is a specific record, measurement, or date the reviewer needed and did not have, I will work with Dr. Reyes's office to get it to you promptly.

### 6. Additional clinical context

My records also document that I have **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.**

---

### What I am asking for

I respectfully ask that the plan:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize the lumbar disc decompression (CPT 63030) as recommended by Dr. Reyes;
2. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician reviewer with relevant expertise in spine surgery;
3. Provide me, at no charge, with a copy of the specific clinical criteria and the reviewer's rationale used in both the original determination and this appeal; and
4. Identify in writing any specific documentation still needed, so my surgeon can supply it.

Per the notice dated August 23, 2026, my appeal must be received within 180 days of that date — **by February 19, 2027** — and I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on that denial letter. If a different form or submission channel is needed for this appeal to be processed, please let me know and I will resubmit promptly.

I have been living with this pain for two years. I have done the physical therapy, taken the medication, and had the injection, and I am still unable to stand for more than ten minutes. I would be grateful for a careful second look at my records alongside the plan's own policy.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Morgan Foster**
